text.p: Mannesmann Arcor, the German telecommunications group, said on Tuesday it had filed a complaint with the German government against monopoly Deutsche Telekom AG over the prices it is charging to allow rivals to access its networks.

Mannesmann's complaint is the first to target the prices that Telekom has been charging for allowing rivals to use its monopoly network to reach customers in local networks. The industry has alleged that Telekom's prices were well above internationally accepted levels.
"The conditions in the offer from Telekom are not cost-oriented," a Mannesman Arcor spokeswoman said.

The new complaint comes a week after the Post and Telecommunications Ministry ordered Telekom to provide rivals the possibility to connect to its monopoly network in a so-called unbundled interconnection.
The ministry confirmed that it had received the complaint from Mannesman Arcor and said German law now requires it to decide on the matter within 10 weeks.

Because most new telecoms companies gearing up for full competition in the sector on January 1, 1998 do not own substantial networks of their own, they must rely on being able to use Telekom's network to gain access to their own customers.
The cost of accessing Telekom's local network is the key factor that could make or break a company's bid to compete once markets are liberalised.
